cities.name: Tirumala
cities.overview: A temple town on the seven hills above Tirupati, run by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams and visited by tens of thousands of pilgrims every day.

cities.name: Araku Valley
cities.overview: A hill valley in the Eastern Ghats about 115 km from Visakhapatnam, known for coffee estates, tribal culture and the scenic train ride up from the coast.

cities.name: Lepakshi
cities.overview: A small village in Sri Sathya Sai district, about 120 km from Bengaluru, built around one of the finest Vijayanagara-era temples in Andhra Pradesh.

cities.name: Visakhapatnam
cities.overview: Andhra's largest city and a naval port, set between the Eastern Ghats and golden beaches.
cities.history: An old trading port that grew under the British and became the headquarters of India's Eastern Naval Command.

cities.name: Vijayawada
cities.overview: A busy river city on the Krishna, near the new state capital region and the Buddhist site at Amaravati.

cities.name: Tirupati
cities.overview: The city at the foot of the Tirumala hills, one of the world's busiest pilgrim centres.

cities.name: Rajahmundry
cities.overview: A city on the Godavari, gateway to the Papikondalu hills and the Konaseema delta.

cities.name: Kadapa
cities.overview: A Rayalaseema city, close to the gorge at Gandikota.

cities.name: Kurnool
cities.overview: A city on the Tungabhadra, the base for the Belum Caves and Srisailam.

cities.name: Kakinada
cities.overview: A Godavari delta port close to the mangroves of Coringa.

cities.name: Madanapalle
cities.overview: A hill country town in the south, close to Horsley Hills.

cities.name: Guntur
cities.overview: A chilli market city close to Amaravati and the Nagarjunakonda dam.

places.name: Sri Venkateswara Temple, Tirumala
places.shortDescription: One of the most visited Hindu shrines in the world, dedicated to Lord Venkateswara on the Tirumala hills.
places.description: The temple of Lord Venkateswara, a form of Vishnu, sits on Venkatadri, one of the seven peaks of the Tirumala hills. Pilgrims climb the hills on foot by the Alipiri steps or travel up the ghat road from Tirupati, and many offer their hair at the tonsuring halls as a vow. The gold-plated Ananda Nilayam vimana rises over the sanctum, and the temple's laddu prasadam is famous across India. Darshan is free in the general queue; paid special-entry slots must be booked in advance on the TTD website.
places.history: The temple's origins are ancient, and inscriptions from the Pallava, Chola, Pandya and Vijayanagara periods record gifts to the shrine. The Vijayanagara emperor Krishnadevaraya visited several times in the 16th century and his statue stands inside the temple.
places.bestTimeNote: September to February is coolest. The Brahmotsavam festival (usually September–October) draws very large crowds.

entryFee.note: Free general darshan; ₹300 special-entry darshan bookable online. Check tirumala.org.

timings.hours: Open almost round the clock; darshan slots are allotted through the day

places.name: Borra Caves
places.shortDescription: Million-year-old limestone caves in the Ananthagiri hills, among the largest and deepest cave systems in India.
places.description: The Borra Caves are a vast karst cave system in the Ananthagiri hills of the Eastern Ghats, about 30 km before Araku. Lit walkways lead down into chambers full of stalactites and stalagmites that locals have named after shapes they resemble, and a small Shiva shrine sits inside. The Gosthani River, which helped carve the caves, flows nearby. The Kirandul passenger train from Visakhapatnam stops at Borra Guhalu station, making the caves an easy halt on the way to Araku.
places.history: The caves were documented in 1807 by William King of the Geological Survey of India. Tribal villagers had long known them, and a local legend tells of a cow that fell through a hole in the roof and led herders to the Shiva lingam inside.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. The caves are cool all year, but the road and valley are at their best after the monsoon.

entryFee.note: Small entry fee with extra charges for cameras; set by APTDC.

location.address: Borra Caves Road, Ananthagiri Mandal, Alluri Sitharama Raju district, Andhra Pradesh 531149

highlights: Kirandul train through the Eastern Ghats

places.name: Veerabhadra Temple, Lepakshi
places.shortDescription: A 16th-century Vijayanagara temple with a hanging pillar, vivid ceiling frescoes and a giant monolithic Nandi.
places.description: Built on a low granite hill shaped like a tortoise, the Veerabhadra Temple is a treasure of Vijayanagara art. Its mandapa ceilings carry some of the best-preserved murals of the period, showing scenes from the epics in natural colours. One pillar in the dance hall famously does not touch the floor fully, and visitors slide cloth beneath it. A short walk away, a Nandi carved from a single rock, about 4.5 m high and 8 m long, is among the largest in India.
places.history: The temple was built around 1530 by the brothers Virupanna and Viranna, governors under the Vijayanagara king Achyuta Deva Raya. It is a protected monument of national importance under the Archaeological Survey of India.
places.bestTimeNote: October to February, ideally early morning before the rock heats up.

location.address: Lepakshi, Sri Sathya Sai district, Andhra Pradesh 515331

places.name: Kailasagiri
places.shortDescription: A hilltop park in Visakhapatnam with a cable car, giant Shiva and Parvati statues and sea views.
places.description: Well laid-out gardens on a hill above the bay, reached by road or cable car. A toy train runs round the top.

places.name: RK Beach
places.shortDescription: The main city beach of Visakhapatnam, close to a submarine museum and a war memorial.
places.description: A long curve of sand lined with cafes. The decommissioned submarine INS Kursura, now a museum, stands right on the shore.

places.name: Simhachalam Temple
places.shortDescription: A hilltop temple of Varaha Narasimha near Visakhapatnam, with fine Chalukya-style stone carving.
places.description: A busy hill temple 300 m above sea level, where the idol stays covered in sandalwood paste for most of the year.

sources.title: Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha temple, Simhachalam – Wikipedia

places.name: Bheemunipatnam
places.shortDescription: An old Dutch port north of Visakhapatnam, with a quiet beach and a Dutch cemetery.
places.description: A calm beach at the mouth of the Gosthani River. Old Dutch graves and a lighthouse tell of its trading past.

places.name: Undavalli Caves
places.shortDescription: A rock-cut cave temple near Vijayawada, four storeys cut from one hill, with a giant reclining Vishnu.
places.description: A monolithic four-storey block looks over the Krishna valley. Inside is a huge recumbent Vishnu, carved from one single block of granite.

places.name: Kanaka Durga Temple
places.shortDescription: A major goddess temple on Indrakeeladri hill above the Krishna River.
places.description: Pilgrims climb steps or take a lift for the view over the barrage. The Dussehra festival here is huge.

places.name: Prakasam Barrage
places.shortDescription: A long barrage across the Krishna River at Vijayawada, a popular evening spot.
places.description: A 1.2 km barrage that feeds the canals of the delta, with a road across and lights in the evening.

places.name: Kondapalli Fort
places.shortDescription: A hill fort near Vijayawada, in a village known for its wooden toys.
places.description: A large fort on a hill, with a restored gate and palace ruins. The village below makes the famous painted softwood Kondapalli toys.

places.name: Amaravati Stupa
places.shortDescription: A ruined Buddhist stupa on the Krishna River, source of one of ancient India's great sculpture styles.
places.description: Little stands on the site now apart from a low mound, but the small museum beside it holds fine carved limestone panels.
places.history: Probably built in phases from the 3rd century BCE.

places.name: Nagarjunakonda
places.shortDescription: A Buddhist site moved to an island in the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir, reached by boat.
places.description: When the dam was built, monuments were moved to higher ground, and the hilltop became an island. A museum holds the finds.

places.name: Srikalahasti Temple
places.shortDescription: A great Shiva temple at Srikalahasti, near Tirupati, representing the element of air.
places.description: A huge temple on the river, with a white gopuram that's been rebuilt after it collapsed in 2010. People come for the Rahu-Ketu rituals.

places.name: Chandragiri Fort
places.shortDescription: An old Vijayanagara stronghold near Tirupati, with a palace museum.
places.description: A hilltop citadel and a palace, the Raja Mahal, that's now a small museum, near Tirupati. It was a late capital of Vijayanagara.

places.name: Talakona Falls
places.shortDescription: The highest waterfall in Andhra Pradesh, in the Seshachalam hills near Tirupati.
places.description: A forest track leads to the falls, which drop about 80 m. It's within a biosphere reserve, and the area is known for red sanders trees.

places.name: Pulicat Lake
places.shortDescription: India's second-largest brackish lagoon, on the Andhra and Tamil Nadu coast, known for flamingos.
places.description: A wide shallow lagoon behind Sriharikota. Winter brings large flocks of flamingos and waders.

places.name: Araku Valley
places.shortDescription: A green hill valley 111 km from Visakhapatnam, known for coffee, tribes and a scenic train.
places.description: The train from Vizag passes through tunnels to reach coffee estates. The Borra Caves are on the way, and there's a tribal museum.

places.name: Papikondalu
places.shortDescription: A range on the Godavari where boats pass through a gorge, near Rajahmundry.
places.description: A long boat trip through the hills from near Rajahmundry is the classic outing. The national park here has been affected by the Polavaram dam works, so check conditions.

places.name: Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: India's third-largest mangrove forest, on the Godavari delta near Kakinada.
places.description: A boardwalk through the mangroves leads into a quiet world of crabs, otters and waterbirds.

places.name: Gandikota
places.shortDescription: The Grand Canyon of India: a fort above a red gorge on the Penna River in Kadapa.
places.description: A red rock gorge beneath ancient walls, with a temple and a mosque inside the fort. The sunrise view over the canyon is unforgettable.

places.name: Belum Caves
places.shortDescription: The second-largest cave system on the Indian subcontinent, at over 3 km, in Nandyal district.
places.description: A lit path leads you through stalactites, tunnels and a deep underground stream. Old Jain and Buddhist relics have been found here.

places.name: Srisailam
places.shortDescription: A Shiva Jyotirlinga in the Nallamala forest, on the Krishna River, with a big tiger reserve nearby.
places.description: A forest road takes you to the Mallikarjuna temple, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, in the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve. The Srisailam Dam is close.

places.name: Horsley Hills
places.shortDescription: A small, quiet hill station in Annamayya district at 1,265 m, on the Karnataka border.
places.description: A hill resort with eucalyptus and a small zoo, named after a British collector. It's a good break from the hot plains.
